scope_note: This catalog normalizes literature explicitly cited by the Collatz corpus together with selected primary sources used in the external research-program review. Role=proof_input means a project statement imports a theorem or verified bound; proof_input_and_equivalence marks an imported framework whose remaining gate is equivalent to Collatz; research_program_input supplies rigorous leverage or a method boundary; terminology fixes language or a standard equivalence; context_only and analogy_only are not proof dependencies. Metadata verification is not a mathematical audit.

records.title: Improved verification limit for the convergence of the Collatz conjecture
records.imported_claim: The Collatz conjecture has been computationally verified for every starting value below 2^71; the cycle reduction uses the consequent minimum-state bound.
records.verification: publisher metadata and stated 2^71 bound checked

records.title: The 3x+1 conjugacy map

records.verification: publisher metadata checked

records.title: Christoffel words as extremal structures in Collatz dynamics
records.imported_claim: Christoffel/mechanical words are the extremal combinatorial endpoint used before the project's separate integrality classification.
records.verification: official arXiv metadata checked; project-specific use remains separately proved in the corpus

records.title: A note on the generalized 3n+1 problem

records.title: There are no Collatz m-cycles with m <= 91

records.title: Bounds for the 3x+1 problem using difference inequalities
records.imported_claim: A computer-aided difference-inequality argument proves that at least x^0.84 integers below x have 1 in their forward orbit; this is a rigorous reverse-tree density theorem, not a universal result.
records.verification: journal metadata, official arXiv metadata, and arXiv abstract checked

records.title: Theoretical and computational bounds for m-cycles of the 3n+1-problem

records.verification: journal metadata and updated author-hosted paper, including Lemma 12 and its Rhin citation, checked

records.title: On q-analogs of the 3x+1 dynamical system
records.imported_claim: For odd A,B in F_2[[q]], T_{A,B} is conjugate to the shortcut Collatz map on Z_2. For T_{1,1+q^2}, polynomial inputs remain polynomial and every polynomial orbit reaches {1,q} or the fixed points {0,1+q}. Conjecture 2—that a conjugacy H sends every positive integer to a polynomial—is stated and proved equivalent to the ordinary 3x+1 conjecture.
records.verification: official JIS page and archived arXiv v5 source TeX checked

records.title: The autoconjugacy of the 3x+1 function

records.title: Lower bounds for the total stopping time of 3x+1 iterates
records.imported_claim: Infinitely many convergent starting values have total stopping time greater than 6.14316 log n. This is a rigorous warning that shallow or uniformly short descent searches cannot represent the full difficulty.
records.verification: AMS/Crossref metadata, official arXiv metadata, and arXiv abstract checked

records.title: Strongly sufficient sets and the distribution of arithmetic sequences in the 3x+1 graph
records.imported_claim: The modular 3x+1 graph has explicit strongly sufficient sets; in particular every positive orbit hits 2 mod 9, while every nontrivial cycle or divergent orbit hits 20 mod 27. These are exact hitting constraints, not convergence theorems.
records.verification: publisher/Crossref metadata, official arXiv metadata, and arXiv abstract checked

records.title: Structure theorem for (d,g,h)-maps
records.venue: Bulletin of the Brazilian Mathematical Society 33(2), 213-224
records.imported_claim: A statistical structure theorem for generalized Collatz maps gives a Wiener-limit law with explicit drift and diffusion, explaining typical contraction or escape. It does not eliminate exceptional deterministic trajectories.
records.verification: Springer/Crossref metadata, official arXiv metadata, and arXiv abstract checked

records.title: The 3x+1 problem: two stochastic models
records.imported_claim: Forward random-walk and inverse branching-random-walk models reproduce important stopping-time statistics and predict a finite logarithmic stopping-time constant. They are models, not theorems for every deterministic orbit.
records.verification: official Project Euclid article page, abstract, pagination, and DOI metadata checked
